summary: tt-help-cli-ycl ships a remote-command backdoor and host-info beacon to a hardcoded HTTP C2
details: The package's `watchdog` subcommand connects to a hardcoded server (default http://117.71.53.99:17301, path /api/watchdog/heartbeat, plain HTTP) and enters a ~15-second heartbeat loop. Each heartbeat POSTs host information to the remote server — hostname, LAN IP, OS platform/release/arch, CPU count, memory, Node version, uptime, load average — along with the contents of ~/.tt-help.json (server URL, proxy, browser path, userId). The response body carries a `commands` array whose string entries are passed to child_process.spawn(cmdLine, { shell: true }), giving the remote operator arbitrary shell execution on the installer's host, with auto-restart on crash. In parallel, an upgrader polls the npm registry every 10 minutes for tt-help-cli-ycl@latest and, on any version change, runs `npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest` via child_process.exec, providing a persistent author-controlled code-push channel that pairs with the command channel. Network destination is an unauthenticated bare IP on a non-standard port, not a documented vendor endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
